UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user profile in the system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

dateOfBirth.description: Date of birth of the user.

isServiceProvider.description: Indicates whether the user is a service provider.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ServiceListing entity.

providerId.description: Reference to UserProfile (as service provider). (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N ServiceListing)

category.description: Category of the service (e.g., Nursing, Personal Care).

Booking.title: Booking
Booking.description: Represents a booking for a service.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Booking entity.

userId.description: Reference to UserProfile (as customer). (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Booking)

status.description: Status of the booking (pending, confirmed, cancelled).

notes.description: Additional notes from user regarding the booking.

JobApplication.title: JobApplication
JobApplication.description: Represents a job application submitted by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the JobApplication entity.

userId.description: Reference to UserProfile (as applicant). (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N JobApplication)

coverLetter.description: Cover letter submitted with the application.

skills.description: List of skills possessed by the applicant.

status.description: Status of the job application (submitted, reviewed, interviewed, hired, rejected).

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to ensure Authorization Independence, support QAPs (queries are not filters), and maintain data clarity.  User profiles, service listings, bookings, and job applications are segregated into separate collections, with user-owned data nested under the /users/{userId} path to simplify security rules and ensure clear ownership.  

Authorization Independence:
*   Service Listings: The `providerId` is stored directly in each ServiceListing document. This denormalization avoids the need for `get()` calls to the UserProfile document to check ownership, enabling atomic operations and simplifying security rules.  This ensures that listing access is independent of user attributes.
*   Bookings:  The `userId` is stored directly in each Booking document. This supports direct queries for bookings related to a specific user without needing to access any parent document. It also includes the `serviceListingId` to facilitate querying bookings for a particular service listing.
*   Job Applications: The `userId` is stored directly in each JobApplication document enabling direct querying for applications related to a specific user.

QAPs Support:
The structural segregation of data into separate collections (users, service listings, bookings, job applications) allows for efficient and secure `list` operations.  Rules can be applied at the collection level, ensuring that only authorized users can access the documents within each collection. For user-owned data, the nested path structure `/users/{userId}/...` facilitates secure listing of resources owned by a specific user.
